hypotheses.mechanism_label: Confined acid-water network with VTF-governed hybrid hopping
hypotheses.description: Proton transport occurs in a continuous phosphoric-acid/water network confined within and between attapulgite fibrous channels, where structural relaxation of the hydrogen-bond network controls mobility. The dominant conductivity variation is set more by how much connected liquid-like carrier medium is loaded into the host (N) than by the acid/water ratio R alone, while a low-temperature dynamical arrest produces an apparent breakpoint.
hypotheses.key_prediction: When N is increased at fixed R, conductivity should rise strongly with only modest change in fitted activation energy, and the temperature dependence should remain predominantly VTF-like with a crossover near the observed breakpoint window rather than switching to a truly different transport mechanism.

hypotheses.mechanism_label: Two-population bound-water crossover with piecewise proton transport
hypotheses.description: The carrier medium comprises at least two confined acid-water populations in attapulgite: a more weakly bound, higher-mobility population and a more strongly bound interfacial population. Above the breakpoint, proton motion uses a mixed hopping/vehicular pathway through the weakly bound network; below it, transport becomes dominated by the strongly bound population and shows a much higher apparent activation barrier.
hypotheses.key_prediction: Independent probes of water state should reveal two distinct confined populations, and samples with a larger fraction of weakly bound acid-water should show both higher room-temperature conductivity and a sharper transport crossover near 230-240 K.

hypotheses.mechanism_label: Interfacial proton hopping on acid-decorated attapulgite surfaces
hypotheses.description: Most protons move along interfacial hydrogen-bond chains anchored to attapulgite surface groups and adsorbed phosphate species, rather than through a bulk-like liquid channel. In this view, N mainly tunes the extent and connectivity of wetted surface pathways, while R has weak influence because excess acid changes speciation more than it creates new interfacial hopping sites.
hypotheses.key_prediction: Conductivity should scale more strongly with accessible clay surface wetting/connectivity than with total free liquid content, and spectroscopic signatures of strongly adsorbed phosphate/water should correlate better with sigma than bulk acid composition does.

hypotheses.mechanism_label: Loading-driven percolation of confined acid domains with VTF relaxation
hypotheses.description: The dominant physics is a percolation-like increase in connectivity of confined acid-water domains as liquid loading N increases within the attapulgite matrix. Once a connected network forms, proton transport is liquid-like and relaxation-coupled (VTF), while the low-temperature breakpoint reflects partial loss of percolation through freezing or immobilization of the most mobile links.
hypotheses.key_prediction: There should be a sharper conductivity gain versus N near a connectivity threshold than versus R, and below the breakpoint the effective conducting fraction should collapse more than the intrinsic mobility of the remaining phase.

reasoning_notes: The hypotheses compete mainly on transport mode (hybrid hopping/vehicular vs interfacial Grotthuss vs ionic-liquid-like), phase structure (continuous phase vs percolative confined domains vs interfacial core-shell), and interpretation of the breakpoint (relaxation crossover within one confined population vs exchange between strong/weak bound populations). VTF dominance strongly motivates relaxation-coupled pictures, while the breakpoint and split activation energies leave room for a two-population confined-medium hypothesis.
